prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 公式文本 · 物理量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "物理量" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 2: header "符号" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "公式" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 91px
  col 4: header "单位" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 274px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1A: widths [66, 52, 86, 52, 103] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [66, 52, 90, 52, 99] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [66, 54, 86, 54, 99] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [69, 51, 90, 51, 98] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [82, 51, 77, 51, 98] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 1
Design r2C: widths [66, 51, 93, 51, 98] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 3/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [67, 52, 90, 52, 98] · table 360×368px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [66, 52, 91, 52, 98] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3A"],"acceptable":["r3B","r1B","r1C","r1A","r2A","r2C"],"bad":[{"design":"r2B","why":"公式列仅 77px，正文只剩 56px，小于 65px 的不可断词 G·m₁m₂/r²，导致 r² 被拆到下一行；公式被拆断，读者容易误读。"}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[67,71],[52,54],[86,90],[52,54],[98,102]],"rationale":"r3A 是唯一让 5 个表头全部单行显示的方案，同时没有公式或单位串被拆断，因此表格高度从 392px 降到 368px。它把第一列压到 67px 的临界值，把说明列压到 98px 的临界值，正好保住“物理量”和 77px 的长数字/单位串，同时把省下的宽度给公式列。其余方案大多只多包了一个“物理量”表头，仍可发布；r2B 则越过了公式列的不可断词下限，属于明确错误。","principles":{"general":["列宽应由最长不可断词和列的角色决定，而不是平均分配或追求对称。","表头也是内容：短表头只差 1px 就可能换行，并让整行高度翻倍。","公式、编号、数字和单位串必须整块保留；说明性文字可以换行吸收剩余宽度。","在窄屏表格里，消除表头换行往往比给说明列多几像素空白更能改善整体节奏。"],"specific":["说明列至少要 98px，才能容纳 77px 的 6.674×10⁻¹¹ / J/(mol·K) 类串。","公式列至少 86px，才能让 G·m₁m₂/r² 不被拆开；90px 已足够，继续加宽不会减少行数。","符号列和单位列 52px 正好容纳 31px 的双字表头，低于 52px 会把“符号”“单位”拆成单字。","第一列 67px 是“物理量”单行显示的下限，r3A 正是靠这一点取得 0/5 表头换行。"]},"tradeoffs":"可以争论的是：把更多宽度给说明列（如 r1A 的 103px）换取更松的阅读感，是否比 r3A 消除“物理量”表头换行更重要；另一派则愿意接受 r2A/r2C 把“符号”“单位”竖排，以换取正文列宽。","uncertain":"双字表头竖排（r2A/r2C）在正式出版物中是否可接受，取决于刊物对表头整齐度的要求；此外，67px 的第一列对当前四行内容刚好，但换成更长的物理量名称时会很快变高。"}
